[b]Trouble in the East: December 14th, 2026[/b]

Anton Luschek woke up early to a call from his boss on a secure phone. It was 5am, the sun had yet to come peaking up over the Andrudin skyline, into his 5th story apartment. He rolled over in his bed, grabbing his phone from the bedside table.

[i]Luschek speaking.[/i]

The voice on the other line stayed quiet before erupting from the phones tiny speaker, [i]So Ive been told, Luschek, that a recent shipment has been killing our clientele. Care to tell me what you know?[/i]

[i]I mean,[/i] he sat up in his bed, running a hand through his thinning hair, [i]I cant tell you much, I didnt have anything to do with it. My job is blindness, maybe moving a small cut if I have to, but Im not one of your importers, Im not responsible.

Wrong. 137-26-HV came through your jurisdiction for distribution. Tell me something about it, or,[/i] three sharp knocks came from the door, [i]I can come in for a chat.

Woah, are you outside? Ill talk, Ill talk.[/i] He sat on the edge of his bed, watching the silhouette in his window. He felt around the room for a piece while trying to keep his boss from getting suspicious. He found it, held the barrel to the curtain, where the faint shadow of his boss was, and fired.

   

[i]I dunno sarge,[/i] a tired officer mumbled into her walkie, [i]I got Luschek here, looks like hes on somethin. Or hes crying on the floor of dispatch about names and clemency for a good, sober reason. You should come down to check it out.[/i]

Sergeant Yiurikov of the APD arrived at dispatch within the hour, ready to talk with Anton. He received a list of names from the officer, obtained from his former boss. It would have to move to the hire-ups, but Luschek could avoid charges for his cooperation. News, however, moved fast. Word of what happened to his boss spread through the Syndicate, out to their suppliers. The supplier list contained names from Vespurias, the ULR, and Dakshina. A few senior APD detectives were assigned to start looking with the help of the KVNA (Koranvistan Valley Narcotics Agency).

[spoiler=Previous post][quote=koranvistan;60894205][b]Trouble in the East: December 13th, 2026[/b]

Andrudin- The historical Eastern Jewel of Koranvistan- was a sprawling, winding maze of streets, parks, and alleyways. Covered in snow every October like clockwork, it was nestled at a high point in the north Elseyrian valleys. The city had seen the worst of the fighting during the revolution, having acted as the rebels bastion for over 9 months of grueling combat. Throughout early 2026, after the new regime secured a hard-won victory with the aid of several foreign powers ([b]OOC: Reply if you helped in the war, so far the only nation on the list is Corzerran[/b]), a great rebuild was taking place. Destroyed roads were re-routed for better traffic through the city, new businesses and shops were built, and new urban residences were constructed to bring people in. Andrudin slowly became a hub for economic activity once again, filled with working Koranvistanis and other nationals from Elseyr.

December was never a terrible month. Between the winter festivals and [i]Samurov[/i], a pagan holiday from early tradition, December was often a high point for the people. However, a time for gathering and celebration this year was, instead, a time of remembering what was lost the year before. Bars and nightclubs became havens for the tired and heartbroken. Drinks, empty entertainment, and of course: the black market. The drug trade was dominated, in the Orlov district at least, by the Sasanov Syndicate. The Sasanov Syndicate was a notorious crime family, with connections in and around Elseyr, Vespuria, and Western Shamat ([b]OOC: also reply or tg if you want connections with a crime family or smth idk[/b])

And although the Syndicate strives for product quality to keep returning customers, there are never any guarantees. Things slip through the cracks, tests arent properly administered, and problems arise. The first problem came on December 13th, when reporter Auggie Fritz published a story in the [i]Orlov Times[/i]. 13 people had died of suspected overdoses, 14 more were hospitalized. Fritz, in her article, took several statements from those willing and affected by, what seemed to be, contamination.

[i]I dunno what happened, I was doin my normal uh routine, as it was, and den I started seein alla dese spots in my eyes. It was like nothin Id nevah seen, an den I was atta hospital![/i] One anonymous person reported.

[i]I was handling. Nothing big, just a small-time sale every now and again. One of the bags tore open as I was sorting my stock, and I got enough on my hands to cause a problem. Theres no being safe with this, its a danger.[/i] A Syndicate member, also anonymous, spoke. [i]Nobodys okay with this. And if I can go on record here, dead isnt how we want a customer. Happy, a little numb, who cares. You get by how you get by. But this isnt right, and we are gonna get some.. Restitution, lets say, from whoever supplied this.[/i]

The Monarchy has yet to issue an official statement on the matter, but is ...hard at work in an attempt to prevent further issue.
[/quote][/spoiler]

[b]The Sealiph of Irocco, Bearer of the Seal of Interpretation

To Hanniel Magon, First Suffet of [nation=noflag]Qartena Hadasht[/nation]

In the Name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful[/b]

Firstly, I would like to congratulate your state on this recent expansion to re-establish the natural borders of the Ancient Republic of Qartena Hadasht, though the morality of it is questioned by some within my Court. Nonetheless, I understand the struggles of incorporating new people, as a mere twenty-five years ago I annexed the Republic of Sybu. However, we have the boon of their population being much less than ours. As it stands currently, the Assembly of Iyaiids remains suspicious of you; however, the Itiammudian Islamic Airforce, bearing witness to your aircraft's capabilities, has lobbied me during a recent meeting in the Council of National Defence and Offence. Thus, I have reached out to you.

We would like to both enter into diplomatic negotiations with Qartena Hadasht regarding the formalisation of diplomacy, and discuss the purchase of a number of Qartena Hadasht aircraft for the Itiammudian Islamic Airforce. Though, of course, this is all contingent on your response and diplomatic inquiry if we reach that stage. It is believed by myself, and a number of those in both of the 	
Consultative Assemblies and the Council of National Defence and Offence, that entering into relations outside our standard station is wise for the preservation of Pan-Shamatine ideals, and that coagulation with other Shamatine states is wise for the preservation of our sovereignty against these foreigners.

I hope for a swift and positive response to be sent to my station at Imdekka, though we understand if coldness is returned to our offer. 

Peace be upon those who follow the guidance,

Bearer of the Seal of Interpretation,
Sealiph,

	
Ibrahim ibn Gakh'ud Al Iyaiid
